title: Read Secrets from C#
description: Use AWSSDK.SecretsManager to fetch secrets into ASP.NET Core without hardcoding credentials.

data.text: The `AWSSDK.SecretsManager` package lets you read, set, and delete secrets programmatically. In ASP.NET Core, you typically read secrets at startup and inject them as configuration.

data.title: Read a secret from Secrets Manager
data.content: Use `SecretsManagerClient` with the default credential chain. This example includes a full `SecretService` class with caching to reduce API calls.

data.text: ASP.NET Core configuration is a key-value pipeline. You can add a custom provider that reads from Secrets Manager.

data.title: Add Secrets Manager to configuration
data.content: Register a custom configuration provider in Program.cs. Includes try/catch and expected output comments.

data.title: Caching secrets
data.text: Secrets Manager calls are network operations. Cache secrets in memory or distributed cache to avoid throttling and reduce latency.

data.title: Read a database connection string from Secrets Manager
data.description: Move a hardcoded connection string into Secrets Manager and load it in ASP.NET Core.
steps: Add a secret named `aspnet/connectionstrings/default` to Secrets Manager
Add Secrets Manager to the configuration pipeline
Replace hardcoded `GetConnectionString` usage with the new pipeline
Run the app locally and verify the connection string loads
data.expectedOutcome: The app starts, reads the connection string from Secrets Manager, and no secrets exist in appsettings.json.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use a configuration provider for seamless integration with ASP.NET Core
Cache secrets to reduce network calls and avoid throttling
Prefer the default credential chain so the same code works locally and in AWS
data.takeaway: Reading secrets from C# is straightforward once Secrets Manager is wired into the configuration pipeline.
